title: The Euclidean shortest vector problem

problem.name: The Euclidean shortest vector problem
problem.statement_latex: Given a basis $B\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}$ of a rank-$n$ lattice $L=B\mathbb Z^n$, output $v\in L\setminus\{0\}$ minimizing $\|v\|_2$. Exact SVP is the central subroutine in block lattice reduction and lattice cryptanalysis. The comparison uses arithmetic or bit-operation time with polynomial factors in input precision suppressed, and quantum gate time in the stated coherent-memory model; enumeration additionally counts tree-oracle operations.

quantum.headline_latex: $2^{0.247n+o(n)}$ rigorous time, Hhan--Kim--Kim--Laarhoven; $2^{0.2563n+o(n)}$ heuristic time, reusable quantum walks.
quantum.headline_text: $2^{0.247n+o(n)}$ rigorous time, Hhan–Kim–Kim–Laarhoven; $2^{0.2563n+o(n)}$ heuristic time, reusable quantum walks.
quantum.details_latex: The superlattice bound is stated in the November 2026 preprint and has a $2^{0.247n+o(n)}$ quantum time-space bound. The heuristic Bonnetain et al. sieve uses coherent access to exponential lists and the standard random-vector assumptions of lattice sieving. Aono--Nguyen--Shen quantum enumeration instead takes roughly $\sqrt T\,\operatorname{poly}(n)$ operations for a search tree with $T$ nodes, using polynomial quantum workspace. Aggarwal--Chen--Kumar--Shen provide a separate rigorous memory tradeoff: $2^{0.950n+o(n)}$ time with polynomial qubits and exponential classical memory, or $2^{0.835n+o(n)}$ with QRAM.

classical.headline_latex: $2^{0.409n+o(n)}$ rigorous time, Hhan--Kim--Kim--Laarhoven; $2^{0.2925n+o(n)}$ heuristic time, Becker--Ducas--Gama--Laarhoven sieving.
classical.headline_text: $2^{0.409n+o(n)}$ rigorous time, Hhan–Kim–Kim–Laarhoven; $2^{0.2925n+o(n)}$ heuristic time, Becker–Ducas–Gama–Laarhoven sieving.
classical.details_latex: The superlattice algorithm uses $2^{0.259n+o(n)}$ space. The heuristic sieve uses $2^{0.2075n+o(n)}$ space. These are distinct comparisons: the rigorous quantum exponent is paired with the rigorous classical exponent, and the heuristic pair shares its distribution assumptions. Classical enumeration costs $T$ node operations for the specified tree. Input precision contributes polynomial factors to the displayed dimension exponents.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedups through smaller exponential constants in $n$. Enumeration gives a quadratic improvement in tree size through quantum backtracking; quantum walks and amplification accelerate sieve subroutines.

evidence.description_latex: Partial evidence for a separation. Rigorous upper bounds and heuristic sieve estimates have separate assumptions; the superlattice results are stated in a 2026 preprint.

hardware.description_latex: Fast sieves need exponential coherent memory and fault-tolerant access to vector lists. Enumeration uses polynomial logical qubits at greater runtime. The polynomial-qubit BDD construction explicitly separates its quantum workspace from exponential classical memory and QRAM.
